criteria.criterion: A new test in crates/athena-core/src/plan.rs, run with `cargo test -p athena-core plan`, builds a plan in which item B depends on a rejected job with no landed retry. B is absent from `order` and present in `refused` with a reason that names the rejected dependency.
criteria.evidence: I ran it: `a_dependency_on_a_rejected_job_with_no_landed_retry_holds_the_item_and_its_dependents` passed, and all 25 plan tests passed. The test calls `Plan::build_with` with `x` rejected. It asserts that `order` is empty and that `refused` holds `b` with an empty `missing` and a reason containing 'depends on x' and 'rejected'. The test would fail without the rule, because `Plan::build`, which takes no history, still orders `b`. The test asserts that too, as its control case.

criteria.criterion: A new test in the same module shows B is not held and is ordered after the retry once a retry of that job has landed. Run `cargo test -p athena-core plan`.
criteria.evidence: `a_dependency_is_met_once_a_retry_of_it_landed_and_the_item_is_ordered_after_it` passed. It checks five cases. (1) `b` is held before landed r2 is added to the chain x←r1←r2 and ordered after. (2) A landed job that retries a different job leaves `b` held. (3) Looping retry links end, both with and without a landed job in the loop. (4) A rejected retry does not release `b`. (5) When the landed retry `r` is also an open entry, the order is [r, b].

criteria.criterion: A test through the real `athena plan` or drain entry in crates/athena-cli/tests (run with `cargo test -p athena-cli`) shows an item depending on a rejected job listed under the held-back items with the reason, and no longer held after a landed retry is linked.
criteria.evidence: I ran it and it passed in 27.65s. The test uses `drain::plan` (the function main.rs calls for `athena plan`) with `RealSteps` on real records, and checks the output of `display::plan`. A dependency job is actually run to rejected, and the dependent names it in its text. The test then checks four things. (1) The dependent is not in `order`. It is in `refused` with a reason naming the job and 'rejected', the text has a `held` line carrying that reason, and the header says '1 held back'. (2) With the retry queued ('try again on <dep>'), the order is [retry] and the dependent is still held. (3) The retry is run and lands. (4) After that the dependent is ordered, `refused` is empty, there is no `held` line, and the header says '0 held back'.

criteria.criterion: A dependent of a held item is held as well and is not ordered. Existing plan.rs and drain tests pass unchanged: `cargo test`.
criteria.evidence: `a_dependent_of_a_held_item_is_held_too` passed. It orders the entries d→c→b→x(failed) so that the hold loop has to repeat. It asserts that `order` is exactly [e], that `refused` is [d, c, b] with the reasons 'depends on c, which is held back' and 'depends on b, which is held back', and that `b`'s reason names x and 'failed'. The diff edits no existing test: tests/drain.rs is changed only by an appended test, and plan.rs only by added tests. The existing `a_dependency_outside_the_plan_counts_as_done` still passes. findings.summary: The change appends a test to tests/drain.rs, which is not on the expected-deliverables list and is named in Out of scope as 'stay as landed'. The deliverable tests/job_plan.rs was not changed.
findings.evidence: The deliverables list names crates/athena-cli/tests/job_plan.rs, not tests/drain.rs, and Out of scope lists tests/drain.rs among files that 'stay as landed'. The diff only appends one new test and edits no existing line, and the critic accepted this file in the planned demonstrations, because job_plan.rs lacks the needed fixtures.

findings.summary: Only the 'try again on <job>' link counts as a retry. A re-ask with the same text, which scope_guard already links as a successor, does not release dependents.
findings.evidence: `scope_guard::request_records` already computes both `retry_of` and `same_text_as` (a re-ask link) for each request job. `job_history` uses only `retried_job`. If a rejected job's successor was re-asked with the same words instead of 'try again on', and that successor landed, its dependents stay held until the owner intervenes. The accepted reading limits the rule to the existing retry link, so this is not a criterion violation, and the failure is conservative: the item is held with a reason shown. Reusing `request_records` links would cover both cases. The records are absent from the snapshot, so I could not check how 20261030-013143-as0j is actually linked to x4nr.

findings.summary: If reading the records fails, `RealSteps::job_history` silently returns no history, which falls back to the old rule where every outside dependency is met.
findings.evidence: `self.records().map(...).unwrap_or_default()` drops the error without adding a note. A note in the drain report would make the fallback visible.

summary:
The change does what was asked and I'm recommending it pass. With the change, a dependency outside the open items counts as met only when that job landed, or when a landed job is linked to it by a "try again on <job>" request, directly or through a chain of retries. A dependency on a job that was rejected, failed, timed out or went stale, with no landed retry, now holds the dependent item. Anything that depends on a held item is held too. Held items are left out of the order and listed under the plan's held-back items with a `held` line that names the dependency.

The rule lives in `Plan::build_with` in plan.rs. Both `athena plan` and the drain build their plan through it, and they read how earlier jobs ended from the records (`reading::job_history`). The drain works only what is in the plan's order, so it skips held items.

**Tests I ran:**
- `cargo test -p athena-core plan::`: all 25 plan tests passed, including the 3 new ones (held item, released after a landed retry, dependents of a held item held too).
- The new end-to-end test in tests/drain.rs passed. It runs a job to a real rejection, shows its dependent held in the plan output with the reason, then lands a retry and shows the dependent ordered.

Athena's recorded fmt, clippy (-D warnings) and full test runs (1737 tests) passed. The CHANGELOG entry and the doc comments in plan.rs describe the new rule. No config, workflow or records file was touched.

**Findings (none blocks the change):**
- **Scope (minor):** the new end-to-end test was added to tests/drain.rs, not tests/job_plan.rs as the deliverables list said. It only appends a test, and the planned demonstrations accepted that file.
- **Re-asks not counted (minor):** a landed re-ask with the same wording, which Athena already links elsewhere, does not release dependents; only "try again on <job>" does. The records aren't in the snapshot, so I couldn't check how 20261030-013143-as0j is linked to 20261029-142853-x4nr. If it is a re-ask rather than a "try again on" request, 20261029-142858-5c0p will stay held, with the reason shown, until it is released by hand.
- **Silent fallback (nit):** if the records can't be read, the plan quietly falls back to the old rule without saying so.
